results.title: Nebius Hikes AI Cloud Prices 21%, Memory Up 41%
results.author: Dr. Heinrich Vogel
highlights:
Nebius just told its customers that AI compute is not getting cheaper. On September 17, 2026, the Amsterdam-based “neocloud” provider notified users it will raise pay-as-you-go prices for Nvidia GPU instances, AMD CPU capacity, and memory starting October 1, 2026. It’s the company’s second price hike in three months, and this time the increases stretch well beyond GPUs into the CPU and memory tiers that most cloud budgets treat as an afterthought.

The numbers are specific. Nvidia H100 instances rise roughly 17%, H200 climbs 20%, B200 goes up about 19%, and the newest B300 chips take the biggest hit at 21%, according to Yahoo Finance’s report on the Nebius announcement. AMD EPYC Genoa CPU rates jump 25%, and memory pricing rises about 41%, the steepest increase across the board. Investors read it as a sign of tight capacity, not weak demand: Nebius shares (Nasdaq: NBIS) jumped as much as 11.1% in pre-market trading the same day.

...

## What Changed: GPU, CPU, and Memory Rates Broken Down

Nebius sells on-demand access to Nvidia GPUs, AMD CPUs, and memory-backed instances to AI labs and enterprises that don’t want to build their own data centers. The October 1 price sheet touches nearly every tier of that stack, and in October 2026 Nebius priced H200 GPUs at $5.40/hour and B200 GPUs at $8.50/hour. Rather than a single across-the-board percentage, Nebius applied different increases to different chip generations, which is itself telling: the newest, most capacity-constrained hardware got hit hardest.

| Instance type | Price before Oct 1, 2026 | Price from Oct 1, 2026 | Increase |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nvidia H100 (per GPU-hour) | $3.85 | $4.50 | ~17% |
| Nvidia H200 (per GPU-hour) | $4.50 | $5.40 | ~20% |
| Nvidia B200 (per GPU-hour) | $7.15 | $8.50 | ~19% |
| Nvidia B300 (per GPU-hour) | $7.85 | $9.50 | ~21% |
| AMD EPYC Genoa CPU (per vCPU-hour) | Unpublished baseline | $0.015 | ~25% |
| Memory-backed instances | Unpublished baseline | Unpublished | ~41% |

Source: Yahoo Finance and Global Banking & Finance Review reporting on Nebius’s customer notice. For a team running a sustained H100 workload, that 17% translates to an extra $0.65 per GPU-hour, which compounds fast across a multi-GPU training cluster running around the clock.

...

Nebius didn’t invent this pattern in September. Around May 2026, the company already raised on-demand capacity prices by an average of 29% and spot capacity by 51%, according to reporting cited by Yahoo Finance’s coverage of the September announcement. Nebius also updated prices for B300, B200, H200 and H100 GPU virtual machines in June 2026. That means Nebius has now raised prices twice in under half a year, with the spot-market increase in the spring actually exceeding the September GPU hikes in percentage terms.

Reuters framed the September move plainly: Nebius is raising prices because demand for computing power keeps rising faster than supply. That’s a different explanation than “costs went up, so we passed them on.” It’s closer to basic capacity rationing, the same mechanism that pushed cloud GPU rental rates up during the original 2023 H100 shortage, except this time it’s spreading into CPU and memory tiers that used to be treated as commodity add-ons.

...

| Provider | H100 rate (approx., per GPU-hour) | Billing type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RunPod | $1.99 – $2.99 | On-demand / marketplace |
| Lambda | $3.29 – $3.99 | On-demand |
| Nebius | $4.50 (from Oct 1) | On-demand |
| CoreWeave | $4.25 – $6.16 | On-demand |
| AWS (P5, list price) | ~$6.88 (per-GPU basis) | On-demand |
| Google Cloud | Spot from ~$2.25; on-demand higher | Spot / on-demand |

...

Even after the October 1 increase, Nebius’s $4.50 H100 rate, which a comparison published November 4 still lists as its on-demand price per GPU-hour, lands in the middle of the pack, more expensive than RunPod and Lambda, cheaper than AWS’s list price, and roughly comparable to CoreWeave’s range. That positioning matters: Nebius isn’t pricing itself out of the market, it’s raising prices while staying competitive with the hyperscalers, which is exactly the kind of move a provider makes when it believes customers value reliability and available capacity more than shaving a dollar off the hourly rate.

...

### How much more will Nvidia H100, H200, B200, and B300 instances cost on Nebius?

Starting October 1, 2026, H100 rises from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour (about 17%), H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40 (about 20%), B200 rises from $7.15 to $8.50 (about 19%), and B300 rises from $7.85 to $9.50 (about 21%), according to Nebius’s customer notice reported by Yahoo Finance.

results.title: GPU rents rise 17–21% on 1 October while the neoclouds' own loan documents show borrowing 100bp dearer
highlights:
The Thursday news is a broker call and should be labelled as one: JPMorgan's Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to Overweight from Neutral and raised his target to $125 from $120, arguing the company should lean into shorter contracts carrying premium pricing. CoreWeave closed Thursday at $90.13, up 3.72%, and gave it back on Friday. Nebius closed Thursday at $243.48, up 7.44%.

The pricing half of the thesis is verifiable at source, which is the most useful thing here. Nebius's own pricing page carries two columns — current, and effective 1 October 2026 — showing on-demand per-GPU-hour rates going from $3.85 to $4.50 for H100, $4.50 to $5.40 for H200, $7.15 to $8.50 for B200 and $7.85 to $9.50 for B300. Those are increases of 16.9%, 20.0%, 18.9% and 21.0%. Roundups describing this as up to 21% are accurate; the table is better, because it says which chip and from what. It is a rate card, not a revenue disclosure — what Nebius intends to charge, not what it will collect.

results.title: Nebius Raised the Rent 21%.
results.author: ThePortablePortfolio
highlights:
### Nebius told customers its B300 rate goes from $7.85 to $9.50 an hour on Oct 1, the second increase since May. Suppliers sitting on a glut do not send that notice.

ThePortablePortfolio

Sep 23, 2026

The B300 goes from $7.85 an hour to $9.50 on October 1. The H100 goes from $3.85 to $4.50. H200, $4.50 to $5.40. B200, $7.15 to $8.50. Between 17% and 21%, depending on the chip, and it is the second increase Nebius has sent its customers since May.

...

Nebius rallied around 7% in after-hours trading and closed September 18 at $223.54. IREN closed at $46.68, up 7.36% on the day, purely on the inference that scarce capacity can be re-let at higher hourly rates. CoreWeave slipped. That divergence is the interesting part, because the market spent the session sorting operators by who can actually capture a higher rate rather than marking the whole group up together.

The underlying business supports the pricing move rather than contradicting it. Nebius reported second-quarter revenue up 454% to $582.3 million, with AI cloud revenue up 514% to $574.9 million, and adjusted EBITDA swinging to a $236.2 million profit from a $21 million loss a year earlier. Management reaffirmed 2026 revenue guidance of $3.0 to $3.4 billion and expects $7 to $9 billion of annual recurring revenue by year end. In July it secured roughly $775 million of debt financing backed by deployed GPU infrastructure and contracted customer cash flows.

results.title: Nscale Posts $1.02B Net Loss in H1, Nebius GPU Rental Rates Rise Up to 21% | BroadChain.info
highlights:
AI cloud service provider Nebius announced that starting October 1, it will raise on-demand rental prices for some Nvidia GPUs, the second price increase within three months. The price per GPU hour for H100 rose from $3.85 to $4.50, an increase of about 17%; H200 rose from $4.50 to $5.40, an increase of 20%; B200 and B300 rose to $8.50 and $9.50 respectively. This price adjustment also involves some CPU and memory resources. Nebius recently signed four customer contracts averaging more than $1 billion each, and competitor CoreWeave also said prices for newly signed computing power contracts have increased. However, this adjustment targets on-demand quotes for designated regions and models, and long-term reservation customers can still obtain discounts.

 Today's main thread: GPU rental prices are still rising, but the funds needed for computing power expansion are also becoming increasingly massive. Nebius once again raised on-demand quotes, OpenAI expects free cash flow outflow of $278 billion over the next five years, and Oracle-related data center loans are seeing discounts and distribution difficulties. There are still pricing signals on the demand side, but whether projects can obtain funding, be delivered on schedule, and generate revenue will affect subsequent expansion.

results.author: James Okafor
highlights:
# Nebius says it will raise AI cloud rental prices from October 1

The Amsterdam-based neocloud firm's second increase in three months lifts pay-as-you-go rates for selected Nvidia GPUs by 17% to 21%, with memory offerings rising about 41%, though customers reserving large clusters for months can still get commitment discounts.

James Okafor September 19, 2026

Cloud provider Nebius will raise pay-as-you-go prices for leasing selected Nvidia chips starting October 1, the company said on Thursday, September 17, in comments reported by Reuters and carried by Economic Times Tech. It is the company's second price increase in three months. [1]

Rates for selected Nvidia graphics processing units will rise between 17% and 21%, according to the report. On-demand rates for some central processing units made by AMD and Intel, along with memory offerings, are also going up: the company said prices of some CPU-only instances will rise by 25% and memory offerings by about 41%. Customers reserving large-scale clusters for multiple months can receive commitment discounts. [1]

...

The increases follow a quarter of rapid growth in the Amsterdam-based firm's AI cloud business, during which it signed four customer contracts averaging more than $1 billion each. Neocloud companies such as Nebius rent out the high-powered chips and data centre infrastructure used to train and run AI models. Demand for that capacity is surging, per the report, and rival CoreWeave said earlier the same day that it is signing contracts at higher prices. [1]

results.title: Your GPU provider can re-price your workloads with two weeks' notice. Nebius just did — again. | Peter Lee
results.author: Peter Lee
highlights:
On September 17, Nebius told customers that pay-as-you-go GPU rates rise October 1: H100s from $3.85 to $4.50/hr (+17%), B300s to $9.50 (+21%), CPU +25%, and memory-backed instances +41%. It's their second hike in three months.

Two things worth noting:
First, the steepest increase isn't on GPUs — it's memory (+41%). The binding constraint on AI compute right now isn't silicon, it's memory and the megawatts to run it. That's why even four-year-old H100s are getting more expensive to rent, not cheaper.

Second, the market loved it. NBIS jumped ~9% on the news. Investors read it as pricing power — capacity rationing, not distress. When your customers have nowhere else to go, you can move the rate card twice a quarter.
This is the FinOps lesson I keep coming back to: in GPU land, price predictability is becoming a genuine differentiator. The cheapest $/GPU-hr means nothing if the number changes before your budget cycle ends.

results.title: Nebius Is Raising GPU Prices Again — the Signal Behind the Stock Jump | AInvest
results.author: Adrian Hoffner
highlights:
Aime Summary

- Nebius NBIS-- raised GPU/CPU cloud prices 17-41% in October, driving a 6% stock surge as peers rose 3-4%.

- Price hikes reflect market demand for scarce AI chips, with B300/H100 hourly rates now $9.50-$4.50.

- $775M secured debt and $1B+ contracts with Microsoft/Meta validate capacity scarcity and pricing power.

- Future profitability hinges on sustaining chip scarcity amid potential oversupply from Nvidia NVDA-- or client discounts.

Nebius is raising rent on the scarcest hardware in tech 861077-- — for the second time in three months. On September 17 the Amsterdam-based neocloud said it will lift pay-as-you-go prices on its Nvidia NVDA-- GPU and CPU cloud services effective October 1, hiking rates on selected Nvidia chips by 17% to 21%, CPU-only instances by 25%, and memory offerings by roughly 41%. Shares rose about 6% in overnight trading, and neocloud peers CoreWeave and IREN followed by 3% to 4%. The reflex is to file this under "another AI stock popping on momentum." The price list says it is the opposite of hype.

A price hike on a neocloud is a spot-market repricing of scarce capacity. Nebius NBIS-- buys Nvidia's newest chips by the ten thousand, wraps them in data centers, and rents the computing out by the hour. The setting of new hourly rates is the company deciding what the open market will now pay for a B300 hour or an H100 hour, the way a hotel reprices rooms in high season. The new numbers carry the point. A B300, Nvidia's newest Blackwell card, goes to $9.50 an hour from $7.85. An H100 moves to $4.50 from $3.85. For a customer renting thousands of hours, that is a meaningful step in cost; for Nebius, on capacity that is already built and paid for, nearly all of it flows to the bottom line.
